newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-SELES STILL CHASING ELUSIVE 1997 TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES STILL CHASING ELUSIVE 1997 TITLE.

text.p: Monica Seles, accustomed to ending a season with a string of titles even after her two-year absence from the circuit, is in the unusual position at the French Open of still seeking her first triumph of 1997.
But the American's love of grand slam events is such that she could yet upset the form book at Roland Garros, where she won three times in a row in the early 1990s.
"I love the grand slams and I'm feeling strong and consistent," third seed Seles said after her 6-3 7-5 second round victory over France's Sarah Pitkowski on Thursday.
"(But) to win this tournament, I'll have to play better tennis than I have for the last two months," she said. "There are no easy matches from now on. I must raise the level of my game."

Seles, back after more than two years out of the game after being stabbed in Hamburg in April 1993, won five titles in 1996 -- out of a career total of 38 -- starting with her fourth Australian Open crown.

But this year, Seles missed out on defending her title in Australia because of a broken finger. The best the 24-year-old has managed with almost half the year over is losing finalist in three tournaments, including Madrid last week.
Seles' backhand looked stronger than her forehand during the match and she is still being troubled by tendinitis in her shoulder.
There is also the added concern for the former world number one that her father is extremely ill and no longer able to give her the support he used to.
"He's my dad and my coach. It's two things taken out of your life," Seles said. "If I'm struggling, I can still talk to him.
"But I have a friend, Claudio, who is helping me through to Wimbledon," she said, referring to Italian former tour player Claudio Pistolesi.
